fields.meta_description: Build a creative request form that changes its questions with each deliverable and flags rush due dates before work starts. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Creative Request Form That Hands Designers a Full Brief
fields.hero_description: Get a creative request form that asks each deliverable's specs up front and saves every request to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What a Designer Needs Before the First Draft
fields.features_subheading: Designers start from a complete brief instead of a chat thread. Each request keeps its specs and reference files in one place.
fields.feature_1:
Questions that follow the deliverable

A requester picks print, digital ad, video, or copy first. The form then asks only what that piece needs, such as trim size and quantity for print or running time for video.
fields.feature_2:
A lead time the form holds to

Set how much notice you need before work starts. A due date inside that window marks the request as a rush, and the requester has to give a reason before it can be sent.
fields.feature_3:
Brand files attached at the start

Requesters upload the logo and any reference pieces with the request. Designers open one record that holds everything, instead of asking for the logo again by email.
fields.feature_4:
Alerts when a request changes hands

The app posts in Slack or sends an email when a request is assigned to a designer or ready for review. A reminder goes out when feedback has waited past the date you set.
fields.feature_5:
Requests you can search later

Each request saves as a row in a database you own, with no response caps. Filter by department or deliverable type to see which groups asked for what work last quarter.
fields.feature_6:
Code you can take with you

On paid plans, export the full code of your creative request app to your GitHub repository. Connect it to the project tool you already use for design work through its API.

faq_plan.q: What is a creative request form?
How do I create a creative request form?

plan.angle: The top 10 is template listings (a work management tool, a form builder, a project tool, a spreadsheet vendor, a public Microsoft form) and two university creative services forms. Each hands the requester one long list of blanks and stops at submit. This page shows a creative request form that changes its questions with the deliverable, flags a due date that is shorter than the team's lead time, turns ad placements into a file list, counts revision rounds, and gives the creative director a queue by designer.
tab_stories: Gwenllian Arbuckle at Vintercroft Community College asks for 60 jazz night posters at 11 x 17 in. with a due date 6 business days out, and because the team asks for 10, the form marks her request as a rush and asks her why.
Kaveh Delgadillo at Haverstock Outfitters picks 3 ad placements for a fall boot sale, and the form turns them into sizes, so with 2 headline versions each the designer receives a list of 6 files.

Aino Mirembe at Solvay Ridge Credit Union has used both included revision rounds on a 30-second auto loan video, and her third round goes to creative director Iskander Hjelm to approve before the editor starts.
Fiammetta Aguilera at Tilbury Freight sees 18 open requests split 8, 6 and 4 across Maks, Ulla and Oskari, and moves 2 of Maks's requests to Oskari so each designer has 6.
